I found two trailing "not X" / "rather than X" clauses.

1. "Access checks default to fail-closed, rather than open." Here "open" is the ordinary antonym of "closed", which anyone would know. The trailer adds nothing, so I cut it.

2. "Those privilege limits are imposed on purpose, rather than by accident." This is the rule's own example of an ordinary-knowledge antonym (on purpose / by accident), so I cut it.

I left "Cybersecurity today is not merely an IT concern; it is a multidimensional discipline…" alone. It is a "not merely X; it is Y" construction, not a trailing clause tacked onto a sentence.

I also left "flag rather than exploit" in the bug-bounty sentence ("report flaws rather than exploit them"). It describes what the ethical hackers do and is built into the sentence, so it is not a bolted-on trailer.

I also left "transform from a reactive posture to one that anticipates…" alone, since it is not a trailing negation.
